title: The judges and the law
summary: In the first year of the judges, the people abide by the laws established by Mosiah, who has died without leaving a successor.

explicit_facts.text: Mosiah had died without leaving anyone to reign in his stead; he had established laws, and the people acknowledged and were obliged to abide by them.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The law-abiding people may be shown in a public setting.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of Mosiah, if depicted in a retrospective image.
The appearance of the people, buildings, and laws.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is narrated background, not a present-time scene of Mosiah's death.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show Mosiah dying or invent a successor.

title: Nehor before Alma
summary: In Alma's first year as chief judge, a large, strong man is brought before him for judgment. The man has preached against the church and advocated popular, supported priests and teachers who need not labor.

explicit_facts.text: A large and notably strong man was brought before Alma in his first year in the judgment seat.
The man had preached against the church and taught that priests and teachers ought to be popular, supported by the people, and not labor with their hands.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nehor stands before Alma in a place of judgment.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of the judgment place and the people who brought him.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: Nehor's earlier preaching is reported; do not depict it as a separate event here.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a trial procedure or dialogue.

title: Nehor's teaching draws support
summary: Nehor teaches his claims about salvation, and many believe him, support him, and give him money.

explicit_facts.text: Nehor taught that all mankind should be saved at the last day and have eternal life, and need not fear or tremble.
Many believed Nehor and began to support him and give him money.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nehor may be shown preaching to listeners who offer him money.
unspecified_visual_details: The place, audience size, clothing, and manner of giving money.

narration.text: all men should have eternal life.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The salvation claim is Nehor's teaching as reported by the narrator, not an endorsed doctrine.
prohibited_inventions: Do not represent the teaching as a visible miracle or divine event.

title: Nehor establishes a church
summary: Nehor grows proud, wears costly apparel, and begins establishing a church according to his preaching.

explicit_facts.text: Nehor became proud, wore costly apparel, and began to establish a church after the manner of his preaching.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nehor may be shown in costly clothing as he begins organizing followers.
unspecified_visual_details: The clothing's exact design and the form or setting of the church.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent named followers or a formal church ceremony.

title: Nehor contends with Gideon
summary: While going to preach to believers, Nehor meets Gideon, a teacher in the church of God. Nehor contends sharply with him, but Gideon withstands him with the words of God.

explicit_facts.text: Nehor met Gideon, a teacher belonging to the church of God, and contended sharply to lead church members away; Gideon withstood him and admonished him with the words of God.
Gideon had been an instrument in delivering Limhi's people from bondage.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The two men may be shown confronting one another.
unspecified_visual_details: The place and any words spoken in their dispute.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: Gideon's role in Limhi's deliverance is background, not a second event to depict.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the deliverance from bondage or invent dialogue.

title: Gideon is slain
summary: Angered by Gideon's resistance, Nehor draws his sword and strikes him. Gideon, weakened by age, cannot withstand the blows and is slain.

explicit_facts.text: Nehor drew his sword and began striking Gideon; Gideon was unable to withstand the blows because of his many years and was slain by the sword.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The sword attack may be depicted without showing wounds or blood.
unspecified_visual_details: The setting and the men's exact appearance.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show gore, blood, or severed body parts.

title: Nehor is brought to Alma
summary: Church members take Nehor and bring him before Alma to be judged. Nehor stands before Alma and pleads boldly for himself.
characters: People of the church of God

explicit_facts.text: The people of the church took the man who slew Gideon and brought him before Alma for judgment.
Nehor stood before Alma and pleaded for himself boldly.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nehor may be shown facing Alma, with church members nearby.
unspecified_visual_details: The identities and appearance of the people who seized him.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent Nehor's plea or other courtroom dialogue.

title: Alma condemns priestcraft
summary: Alma tells Nehor that he is guilty of priestcraft and tried to enforce it by the sword. Alma cites Gideon's death and condemns Nehor to die under Mosiah's law.

explicit_facts.text: Alma said this was the first introduction of priestcraft among the people and accused Nehor of trying to enforce it by the sword, warning of the people's destruction if priestcraft were enforced.
Alma said Nehor had shed the blood of a righteous man who had done much good, and that sparing him would bring the blood upon them for vengeance.
Alma condemned Nehor to die according to the law given by Mosiah and acknowledged by the people.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma may be shown addressing Nehor from the judgment seat.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of the judgment seat and any audience.

spoken_dialogue.text: Therefore thou art condemned to die,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Alma the Younger (high priest)

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Alma's words are the judgment and explanation given in the supplied text.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent additional verdict proceedings or dialogue.

title: Nehor acknowledges his teaching
summary: Nehor is carried to the top of hill Manti, where he acknowledges between heaven and earth that his teaching was contrary to the word of God, and suffers an ignominious death.

explicit_facts.text: Nehor was carried to the top of hill Manti and acknowledged that what he had taught was contrary to the word of God; there he suffered an ignominious death.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nehor and those carrying him may be shown on the hilltop.
unspecified_visual_details: The manner of death and the appearance of those carrying him.

narration.text: what he had taught to the people was contrary to the word of God;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The text does not describe the manner of death.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a specific execution method or depict gore.

title: Priestcraft continues
summary: Nehor's death does not stop priestcraft. Others preach false doctrines for riches and honor, while fearing legal punishment for known lies, theft, robbery, and murder.

explicit_facts.text: After Nehor's death, priestcraft continued to spread; many preached false doctrines for riches and honor.
They dared not lie if it would be known, fearing the law; they pretended to preach according to their belief, and the law could not punish belief.
They dared not steal or rob for fear of the law, and murder was punishable by death.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A preacher addressing listeners may suggest the spread of priestcraft.
unspecified_visual_details: The particular preachers, listeners, locations, and offenses.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: These are summarized conditions, not a specific new crime or trial.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show a specific theft, robbery, murder, or named character.

title: Persecution of church members
summary: People outside the church persecute church members with words because of their humility and their sharing of God's word without payment.
characters: People outside the church of God
People of the church of God

explicit_facts.text: People who did not belong to the church began persecuting those who did and had taken upon themselves the name of Christ.
They afflicted church members with words because of their humility and because they shared the word of God with one another without money or price.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The groups may be shown facing one another while the persecution is conveyed through gestures.
unspecified_visual_details: The words used, the setting, and the identities of the people.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: The source describes affliction with words, not physical attack in this moment.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent insults or depict physical violence in this scene.

title: Contention among church members
summary: Although church law forbids persecution, some members grow proud and contend with adversaries, even striking one another. In Alma's second year, this causes the church affliction and trial.
characters: Proud members of the church of God

explicit_facts.text: Church law forbade members from persecuting nonmembers and forbade persecution among the members.
Many members became proud and contended warmly with adversaries, even coming to blows and striking one another with fists.
In Alma's second year, this caused much affliction and trial for the church.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The fistfight may be shown without graphic injury.
unspecified_visual_details: The identities and number of those fighting.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: The law is background; the described physical action is the members' fighting.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent named fighters or injuries.

title: Some withdraw from the church
summary: Many harden their hearts, have their names blotted out, or withdraw. Those steadfast in faith patiently bear the persecution.
characters: People withdrawing from the church of God
Faithful members of the church of God

explicit_facts.text: Many people's hearts hardened, their names were blotted out and they were no longer remembered among God's people, and many withdrew from the church.
Those who stood fast in faith remained steadfast in keeping God's commandments and patiently bore persecution.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Some people may be shown departing while others remain together.
unspecified_visual_details: How names were blotted out and how the persecution appeared.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: The blotted-out names are reported; avoid inventing a visible supernatural record.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a divine hand or miraculous erasure.

title: Priests and people return to labor
summary: Priests leave their labor to teach, and the people leave their labor to hear. Afterward, all return diligently to their work, with preacher and hearer regarded as equals.
characters: Priests of the church of God
People hearing the word of God

explicit_facts.text: Priests left their labor to teach the word of God, and the people left their labors to hear; afterward all returned diligently to their labor.
The preacher was no better than the hearer and the teacher no better than the learner; all were equal and labored according to their strength.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The scene may show a priest teaching laborers in a setting where work has paused.
unspecified_visual_details: The specific work, teaching place, and appearance of the people.

narration.text: the preacher was no better than the hearer,

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Keep teaching and labor as one narrated cycle, without inventing a specific occupation.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent the words taught or a particular trade.

title: Sharing with those in need
summary: Church members share their substance with people in need, dress neatly without costly apparel, and establish church affairs, leading to continual peace again despite persecution.
characters: People of the church of God

explicit_facts.text: Members shared according to their means with the poor, needy, sick, and afflicted; they did not wear costly apparel, but were neat and comely.
They established the affairs of the church and began to have continual peace again despite persecutions.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Members may be shown sharing goods with people in need.
unspecified_visual_details: The goods shared, clothing designs, and location.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: Peace is a reported condition, not a separate visible event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a specific illness, gift, or persecution episode.

title: Abundance among the church
summary: The church grows exceedingly rich, with abundant animals, grain, precious metals, fine fabrics, and cloth. In prosperity, members provide for people in need without favoring status or church membership.
characters: People of the church of God

explicit_facts.text: The church had abundance of flocks, herds, fatlings, grain, gold, silver, precious things, silk, fine-twined linen, and homely cloth.
They did not send away those lacking clothing, food, drink, nourishment, or who were sick; they were liberal to all in need, regardless of age, status, sex, or church membership.

reasonable_visual_inferences: An abundant supply of goods alongside members sharing with people in need may be depicted.
unspecified_visual_details: The exact goods, garments, and place of distribution.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: The abundance and generosity are reported conditions.
prohibited_inventions: Do not portray wealth as divine reward beyond what the text states.

title: Contrasting conduct and peace
summary: Church members prosper more than nonmembers. The text describes nonmembers' wicked practices and says the law is enforced; offenders become more still, and there is much peace among the Nephites until Alma's fifth year.
characters: People of the church of God

explicit_facts.text: Church members prospered and became wealthier than those outside the church.

The text attributes sorceries, idolatry, idleness, strife, costly apparel, persecution, lying, theft, robbery, sexual immorality, murder, and other wickedness to those outside the church; the law was enforced on transgressors as possible.
As the law was exercised, people suffered according to their deeds, became more still, and dared not commit known wickedness; there was much peace among the Nephites until Alma's fifth year.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A broad view of people living in a settled community may suggest the reported peace.
unspecified_visual_details: Specific offenders, punishments, and the appearance of peace.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: The chapter ends with a narrated summary, not a particular crime or punishment scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a specific act, culprit, punishment, or causal doctrine.
